question: In the biblical creation account in Genesis 1, light was created on the:

options.A: First day

explanation: God said, 'Let there be light' on Day 1; the sun, moon, and stars were set on Day 4.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: According to Genesis 1:26-27, man was created:

options.A: In the image and likeness of God with dominion over creation
options.C: To serve the angels as manual labourers

explanation: Being created in God's image confers unique spiritual dignity, stewardship, and creative moral agency.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The second creation account in Genesis 2 emphasizes that man was formed from:

options.A: The dust of the ground, and God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life
options.D: The branches of the tree of life

explanation: Genesis 2:7 records: 'The Lord God formed man of dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The immediate consequence of Adam and Eve's disobedience in eating the forbidden fruit was:

options.A: Realization of their nakedness, shame, guilt, and spiritual alienation from God
options.C: Immediate elevation to equal status with God

explanation: Their rebellion introduced sin, guilt, fear, broken fellowship with God, and expulsion from Eden.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: When God confronted Adam after eating the forbidden fruit, Adam attempted to excuse himself by:

options.A: Blaming Eve and ultimately God who gave him the woman
options.B: Admitting full personal responsibility and asking for mercy

explanation: Adam deflected blame: 'The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me from the tree, and I ate.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Cain murdered his brother Abel primarily because:

options.A: God had regard for Abel and his offering, provoking Cain's jealousy and wrath
options.C: Abel refused to share his cattle
options.D: Their father Adam ordered them to fight

explanation: Abel offered in faith of the firstborn of his flock; Cain's envious pride led to fratricide.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: God sent the great flood in the days of Noah because:

options.A: The wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and every intent of the thoughts of his heart was evil
options.B: The earth had run out of agricultural farmland
options.D: The builders of Babel were erecting a tower

explanation: Genesis 6 describes widespread corruption and violence provoking divine judgment via the Deluge.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The sign of God's universal covenant with Noah never to destroy the earth with a flood again was the:

options.A: Rainbow in the clouds

explanation: Genesis 9:13: 'I set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The builders of the Tower of Babel were dispersed across the earth because God:

options.A: Confused their language to curb their rebellious pride and self-glorification
options.B: Sent a destructive earthquake that flattened the brick tower
options.C: Sent a plague of poisonous serpents
options.D: Burnt the city with heavenly fire

explanation: Babel symbolized arrogant human autonomy; God scattered them by confounding their speech.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: God called Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees to go to a land He would show him, promising to:

options.A: Make him a great nation, bless him, and bless all families of the earth through him
options.B: Make him the Pharaoh of Egypt
options.C: Give him all the silver mines of Babylon
options.D: Build him a palace of ivory

explanation: Genesis 12:1-3 records the Abrahamic call and the threefold promise of land, descendants, and universal blessing.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The physical token of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants was:

options.A: Circumcision of every male child at eight days old
options.B: Sprinkling of lamb's blood on doorposts
options.D: Building stone altars on mountain peaks

explanation: Genesis 17:10-11 establishes circumcision as the permanent physical seal of the Abrahamic covenant.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Abraham demonstrated supreme faith and obedience when God commanded him to:

options.A: Offer his only son Isaac as a burnt offering on Mount Moriah
options.B: Wage war against the five kings of Sodom
options.C: Return permanently to Ur of the Chaldees
options.D: Sell his cattle herds in Egypt

explanation: Abraham obeyed in faith; God intervened with a ram caught in a thicket, naming the place Yahweh-Yireh.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Esau sold his coveted birthright to his twin brother Jacob for a:

options.A: Bowl of red lentil stew and bread

explanation: Esau despised his spiritual inheritance to satisfy immediate physical hunger, selling his birthright to Jacob.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Jacob had his name changed to 'Israel' after:

options.A: Wrestling all night with an angel of God at Peniel
options.C: Interpreting Pharaoh's seven fat cows dream

explanation: Genesis 32:28: 'Your name shall no longer be Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and with men and have prevailed.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Joseph's jealous brothers originally conspired to kill him in Dothan, but he was sold to:

options.A: Ishmaelite / Midianite merchants travelling to Egypt

explanation: Reuben and Judah intervened to spare his life; Joseph was sold for 20 shekels of silver to traders going to Egypt.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Joseph was elevated to Prime Minister (Vizier) over all Egypt because he:

options.A: Interpreted Pharaoh's dreams of seven fat and seven lean cows with divine wisdom to avert famine
options.B: Led the Egyptian army to conquer Canaan
options.C: Assassinated Potiphar in the royal palace
options.D: Built the great pyramids of Giza

explanation: God gave Joseph understanding of the seven years of plenty and famine, earning Pharaoh's trust.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: God first revealed Himself to Moses while he was tending sheep near Mount Horeb in a:

options.A: Burning bush that burned with fire yet was not consumed
options.B: Violent whirlwind over the Nile river
options.C: Dream of a ladder extending to heaven
options.D: Golden tablet dropped from the clouds

explanation: Exodus 3:2 describes the burning bush where God revealed His sacred name: 'I AM WHO I AM'.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The final tenth plague that compelled Pharaoh to release the Israelites from Egyptian bondage was the:

options.A: Death of all the firstborn of Egypt, both man and beast
options.B: Turning of the Nile river water into blood
options.C: Plague of hail and fire destroying barley crops
options.D: Three days of thick darkness over Egypt

explanation: Exodus 12: Death struck every Egyptian firstborn; Israelites were spared by the blood of the Passover lamb.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: During the Passover, the Israelites were instructed to smear the blood of an unblemished lamb on their:

options.A: Two side doorposts and the lintel of their houses

explanation: The blood served as a sign so the destroying angel would pass over their dwellings.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: God parted which body of water to enable the Israelites to escape from Pharaoh's pursuing chariots?

options.A: The Red Sea

explanation: Moses stretched his staff, east winds parted the Red Sea, and Pharaoh's pursuing army was drowned.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: God gave the Ten Commandments (Decalogue) to Moses on Mount:

options.A: Sinai (Horeb)

explanation: Exodus 20 records the delivery of the moral law on two stone tablets at Mount Sinai.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Which commandment in the Decalogue is accompanied by a specific promise of long life?

options.A: Fifth Commandment ('Honor your father and your mother')
options.B: First Commandment ('You shall have no other gods before Me')
options.C: Seventh Commandment ('You shall not commit adultery')

explanation: Exodus 20:12: 'Honor your father and mother, that your days may be prolonged in the land.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: While Moses was on Mount Sinai receiving the commandments, the Israelites committed idolatry by building a:

options.A: Golden Calf fashioned by Aaron
options.B: Statue of Baal with bronze horns

explanation: Impatience led Aaron and the people to pool gold earrings to mold and worship a golden calf.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Out of the twelve spies sent by Moses to scout the land of Canaan, the two who brought a report of faith were:

options.A: Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh

explanation: Numbers 14: Joshua and Caleb urged trust in God's power, while the ten spread fearful despair.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Moses was barred from entering the Promised Land because he:

options.A: Struck the rock twice in anger at Meribah instead of speaking to it as God commanded
options.B: Refused to lead the army against Jericho
options.C: Lost the two stone tablets of the law
options.D: Refused to ordain Joshua as his successor

explanation: Numbers 20: Moses failed to uphold God's holiness before Israel, viewing Canaan from Mount Nebo before dying.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Who succeeded Moses as the supreme leader of Israel and led them into the Promised Land across the Jordan?

options.A: Joshua

explanation: Joshua was commissioned by God: 'As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The walls of the fortified city of Jericho collapsed after the Israelites:

options.A: Marched around the city once daily for six days, and seven times on the seventh day with trumpet blasts and a loud shout
options.B: Battered the gates with heavy iron rams
options.C: Dug underground tunnels beneath the foundations
options.D: Set fire to the outer wooden fences

explanation: Joshua 6 describes the miracle of Jericho's collapse upon faithful completion of God's instructions.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Deborah the prophetess and judge delivered Israel from the oppression of Jabin King of Canaan with her general:

options.A: Barak

explanation: Judges 4: Deborah summoned Barak to lead troops against Sisera, Canaanite general of King Jabin.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Gideon defeated the massive Midianite army using an army reduced by God to only:

options.A: 300 men who lapped water with their hands like dogs

explanation: God culled Gideon's army to 300 men equipped with trumpets, pitchers, and torches to ensure the glory belonged to God.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Samson lost his supernatural physical strength when:

options.A: Delilah had the seven locks of his hair shaved, violating his Nazirite vow
options.B: He touched the carcass of an unclean swine
options.C: He drank unfermented sweet grape juice
options.D: The Philistines chained him in iron shackles

explanation: Judges 16: Samson's Nazirite consecration resided in his uncut hair; shaving it caused the Spirit to depart.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: When the elders of Israel demanded a king from Prophet Samuel at Ramah, their primary motive was to:

options.A: Be like all the other surrounding Gentile nations and have a king lead them in battle
options.B: Obey an explicit divine commandment in Deuteronomy
options.C: Abolish the high priesthood in Shiloh
options.D: End the payment of agricultural tithes

explanation: 1 Samuel 8: God told Samuel the people had rejected Yahweh as their divine King in demanding human monarchy.

question: The first king anointed over Israel was:

options.A: Saul the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin

explanation: Samuel anointed Saul privately, confirmed later by public lot at Mizpah.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: God definitively rejected Saul from being king over Israel because Saul:

options.A: Disobeyed God's command to utterly destroy the Amalekites by sparing King Agag and the best livestock
options.B: Lost a battle against the Moabites
options.C: Refused to pay gold tribute to the Phoenicians
options.D: Abolished the Feast of Unleavened Bread

explanation: 1 Samuel 15:22: 'To obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed than the fat of rams.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Young David defeated the towering Philistine champion Goliath using:

options.A: A sling, a smooth stone from the brook, and unwavering faith in the name of the Lord of Hosts
options.B: King Saul's heavy bronze armor and iron spear
options.D: A poisoned iron arrow shot from afar

explanation: 1 Samuel 17: David declared: 'You come to me with a sword and spear, but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: When David committed adultery with Bathsheba and murdered Uriah the Hittite, God sent which prophet to rebuke him?

options.A: Nathan

explanation: Nathan told the parable of the rich man who stole the poor man's ewe lamb, confronting David: 'You are the man!'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Which celebrated penitential Psalm did David compose in remorse after his sin with Bathsheba?

options.A: Psalm 51 ('Create in me a clean heart, O God')
options.C: Psalm 91 ('He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High')

explanation: Psalm 51 expresses deep confession, repentance, and plea for spiritual restoration.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: When God appeared to King Solomon in a dream at Gibeon asking what he desired, Solomon requested:

options.A: An understanding heart and wisdom to judge God's people discerningly
options.B: Long life and victory over all external foes
options.C: Vast hoards of gold and silver treasures
options.D: A fleet of trading ships to Ophir

explanation: 1 Kings 3: Solomon sought wisdom rather than wealth or vengeance; God granted wisdom plus unmatched riches and honor.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: King Solomon demonstrated his great judicial discernment in resolving the dispute between two women who:

options.A: Claimed ownership of the same living infant baby boy
options.B: Argued over ownership of an olive vineyard
options.C: Accused each other of stealing gold bracelets
options.D: Fought over a stray donkey in Jerusalem

explanation: Solomon ordered the child cut in two with a sword, identifying the real mother by her willingness to give him up.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The magnificent First Temple in Jerusalem was built by King:

options.A: Solomon

explanation: David gathered materials, but Solomon was chosen by God to build the Temple of the Lord.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In his later years, King Solomon's heart was turned away from wholehearted devotion to Yahweh because:

options.A: His numerous foreign pagan wives led him to build high places for deities like Chemosh and Molech
options.B: He lost his memory due to sickness
options.C: The Queen of Sheba robbed his treasury

explanation: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's foreign marriages seduced him into idolatry, provoking the division of the kingdom.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The United Monarchy of Israel fractured into the Northern Kingdom (Israel) and Southern Kingdom (Judah) under:

options.A: Rehoboam the son of Solomon

explanation: 1 Kings 12: Rehoboam harshly refused tax relief ('My father chastised you with whips, I will with scorpions'), causing 10 tribes to rebel.

question: Jeroboam I, first king of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, established golden calf worship at:

options.A: Dan and Bethel to prevent his subjects from worshipping in Jerusalem

explanation: Jeroboam instituted shrines at Dan and Bethel, fearing Jerusalem pilgrimages would renew loyalty to the House of David.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Prophet Elijah contested the 450 prophets of Baal in a dramatic contest on Mount:

options.A: Carmel

explanation: 1 Kings 18: God answered Elijah's prayer by consuming the drenched sacrifice with heavenly fire, proving 'The Lord, He is God!'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: King Ahab and Queen Jezebel conspired to murder Naboth of Jezreel in order to seize his:

options.A: Family ancestral vineyard situated near the royal palace

explanation: 1 Kings 21: Jezebel hired false witnesses to stone Naboth for blasphemy, prompting Elijah's condemnation of Ahab's house.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Prophet Elijah was taken up into heaven in a:

options.A: Whirlwind with a chariot and horses of fire
options.B: Great sea wave in the Mediterranean
options.C: Cloud over the city of Damascus

explanation: 2 Kings 2:11: 'A chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared... and Elijah went up by a whirlwind to heaven.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Prophet Elisha received a 'double portion' of Elijah's prophetic spirit after:

options.A: Witnessing Elijah being taken up into heaven across the Jordan
options.C: Pouring oil on King Jehu in Ramoth-Gilead

explanation: Elisha asked for a double portion of his master's spirit, confirmed when he saw Elijah's fiery ascension.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Prophet Amos ministered in the Northern Kingdom of Israel, strongly condemning:

options.A: Social injustice, oppression of the poor, dishonest scales, and hollow hypocritical ritualism
options.B: Building wooden bridges over the Jordan

explanation: Amos 5:24: 'Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Prophet Hosea's marriage to Gomer, an unfaithful wife, symbolized:

options.A: God's unconditional, redeeming, and forgiving love for unfaithful Israel
options.B: The destruction of the Egyptian empire
options.C: The wealth of the royal merchants of Tyre
options.D: The holiness of the Temple priesthood

question: Prophet Isaiah received his grand vision and call in the year that:

options.A: King Uzziah died, seeing the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up

options.D: The ark was captured by the Philistines

question: Prophet Jeremiah is frequently referred to as the 'Weeping Prophet' because he:

options.A: Deeply lamented the unrepentant sins of Judah, the destruction of Jerusalem, and the impending Babylonian exile
options.B: Lost all his family members in a shipwreck
options.D: Was banished permanently to the desert of Sin

question: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea during the reign of:

options.A: Caesar Augustus (Roman Emperor) and King Herod the Great

question: Jesus was baptized in the Jordan River by John the Baptist, where:

options.A: The heavens opened, the Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and a Voice declared: 'This is My beloved Son'
options.B: An angel handed Him a golden crown
options.C: The waters of the Jordan ceased flowing for three hours
options.D: The Pharisees bowed down in adoration

question: In the wilderness temptations, when Satan tempted Jesus to turn stones into bread, Jesus answered:

options.A: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God'
options.B: 'I will eat only after forty days have elapsed'

question: The first public miracle performed by Jesus recorded in the Gospel of John was:

options.A: Turning water into wine at the wedding feast in Cana of Galilee
options.C: Feeding the 5,000 with five loaves and two fish

explanation: John 2:1-11: Changing water into wine manifested His glory, prompting His disciples to believe.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In the Sermon on the Mount, the Beatitudes open with: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for:

options.A: Theirs is the kingdom of heaven

syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who proved to be the true neighbor to the assaulted man?

options.A: The Samaritan who showed mercy, bound his wounds, and paid for his inn stay
options.B: The Priest who passed by on the other side
options.C: The Levite who inspected him and hurried away
options.D: The innkeeper who provided free lodging

question: The Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 illustrates:

options.A: The boundless, forgiving love of the Father welcoming home a repentant sinner
options.B: The wisdom of accumulating real estate investments
options.C: The strict obedience of the elder brother
options.D: How to feed swine on a famine-stricken farm

explanation: The father ran, embraced, and threw a celebratory feast for the returned wayward son.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Jesus calmed a violent storm on the Sea of Galilee by saying:

options.A: 'Peace, be still!' and the wind ceased and there was a great calm
options.B: 'Row the boat to the eastern shore!'

question: When Peter made his great confession in Caesarea Philippi saying: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God', Jesus replied that:

options.A: Flesh and blood did not reveal this, but His Father in heaven
options.B: Peter learned this from the high priest Caiaphas

question: At the Transfiguration on the holy mountain, which two Old Testament figures appeared talking with Jesus?

options.A: Moses and Elijah

question: Jesus entered Jerusalem triumphantly riding upon a colt of a donkey, fulfilling the prophecy of:

options.A: Zechariah 9:9

explanation: Zechariah 9:9: 'Behold, your King comes to you, humble and mounted on a donkey, on a colt.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Jesus cleansed the Temple in Jerusalem by driving out moneychangers and sellers of doves, declaring:

options.A: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you are making it a den of robbers'
options.B: 'This building will stand for another thousand years'
options.D: 'You must build another court for the Gentiles'

syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: At the Last Supper, Jesus instituted the Lord's Supper (Holy Communion) using bread and wine to symbolize His:

question: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed in deep agony:

options.A: 'My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me; yet not as I will, but as You will'
options.B: 'Send twelve legions of angels to destroy the Sanhedrin'

explanation: Matthew 26:39: Jesus demonstrated perfect submission to the Father's redemptive will.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Which disciple betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver?

options.A: Judas Iscariot

question: Before the rooster crowed, Apostle Peter denied Jesus how many times?

options.A: Three times

syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The Roman governor who condemned Jesus to be crucified despite declaring Him innocent was:

options.A: Pontius Pilate

syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: On the cross at Golgotha, Jesus cried out in Aramaic: 'Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?', meaning:

options.A: 'My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?'
options.B: 'Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do'
options.D: 'Into Your hands I commit My spirit'

explanation: Mark 15:34: Quoting Psalm 22:1, expressing the terrible weight of bearing the world's sin.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The first witnesses to discover the empty tomb and receive news of Jesus' resurrection on Easter Sunday morning were:

options.A: Mary Magdalene and the other women (Mary mother of James, Salome)
options.C: The eleven disciples assembled in the upper room
options.D: The Roman guards who guarded the sepulchre

syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Before ascending into heaven from the Mount of Olives, Jesus delivered the Great Commission to His disciples, commanding them to:

options.A: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
options.B: Form an army to conquer Rome

question: The promised Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples with tongues of fire and a mighty rushing wind on the Day of:

options.A: Pentecost (Shavuot)

question: Following Peter's powerful Pentecost sermon, how many souls were baptized and added to the church that day?

options.A: About three thousand souls

explanation: Acts 2:41: Peter's proclamation of Christ's resurrection converted about 3,000 souls.

question: Peter and John miraculously healed a man lame from birth at the gate of the Temple called:

options.A: The Beautiful Gate

syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Ananias and his wife Sapphira died suddenly in the presence of Apostle Peter because they:

options.A: Lied to the Holy Spirit by keeping back part of the proceeds of land they sold while pretending to give all
options.B: Refused to attend the Pentecost prayer gathering
options.C: Insulted the Roman governor in Caesarea
options.D: Sold defective wine to the disciples

explanation: Acts 5: Their hypocrisy and deceit against the Holy Spirit brought immediate divine judgment.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The seven deacons in Acts 6 (including Stephen and Philip) were chosen primarily to:

options.A: Oversee the daily distribution of food to Hellenistic widows so the Apostles could devote themselves to prayer and preaching
options.B: Guard the Temple gates against Roman centurions

explanation: Acts 6: The appointment of deacons solved administrative friction and preserved apostolic pastoral priorities.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The first Christian martyr who was stoned to death by the Jewish council while praying for his killers was:

options.A: Stephen

explanation: Acts 7: Stephen saw heaven opened and prayed: 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them' as stones fell on him.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Philip the Evangelist led which foreign dignitary to Christ on the desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza?

options.A: The Ethiopian Eunuch, treasurer of Queen Candace, who was reading Isaiah 53

explanation: Acts 8: Philip explained Isaiah's suffering servant prophecy to the Ethiopian, baptizing him in roadside water.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Saul of Tarsus had his dramatic conversion encounter with the risen Christ while travelling on the road to:

options.A: Damascus, intending to arrest followers of the Way

explanation: Acts 9: A brilliant light flashed and Jesus spoke: 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The Roman centurion Cornelius in Caesarea is historic in Christian history because he was the:

options.A: First Gentile convert baptized by Peter, demonstrating that God shows no partiality
options.B: Officer who nailed Jesus to the cross
options.C: Governor who sentenced Paul to prison
options.D: Soldier who helped Paul escape from Damascus in a basket

explanation: Acts 10: The Holy Spirit fell upon Cornelius' Gentile household, opening the church to the nations.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The disciples of Jesus were first called 'Christians' in the city of:

options.A: Antioch in Syria

explanation: Acts 11:26: Barnabas and Saul taught extensively in Antioch, where believers were first termed 'Christians'.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The Jerusalem Council in Acts 15 met to resolve whether:

options.A: Gentile converts to Christ were required to be circumcised and observe the Law of Moses for salvation
options.B: Women should be allowed to speak Greek in church
options.C: Apostle Peter should be replaced by James
options.D: Christians should pay taxes to the Roman Emperor

explanation: Acts 15: James and the Apostles declared Gentiles saved by grace through faith without circumcision.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In Romans 13:1-7, Apostle Paul teaches that Christians must submit to governing authorities because:

options.A: All authority is instituted by God to maintain public order and punish evildoers
options.B: Rulers will execute all citizens who fail to praise them

explanation: Paul instructs paying taxes, custom duties, and obeying civil magistrates as God's servants for order.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In 1 Corinthians 13, Apostle Paul concludes that of the three theological virtues (Faith, Hope, and Love), the greatest is:

options.A: Love (Agape)

explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:13: 'Now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.'
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In Galatians 5:22-23, the Fruit of the Spirit is listed as:

options.A: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control
options.B: Tongues, prophecy, miracles, healings, and interpretation
options.C: Wealth, health, long life, and earthly fame

explanation: The singular Fruit manifests Christlike character produced by the Holy Spirit in the believer.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In Ephesians 6:10-18, the Whole Armor of God includes which offensive weapon?

options.A: The Sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God

explanation: The sword of the Spirit (God's spoken Word) is the primary offensive spiritual weapon.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In the Epistle of James, faith without works is declared to be:

options.A: Dead

explanation: James 2:17 & 26: Genuine saving faith inevitably produces active righteous works and compassion.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In Philippians 2:5-11 (the Kenosis passage), Apostle Paul exhorts believers to have the mind of Christ, who:

options.A: Humbled Himself, taking the form of a bondservant and becoming obedient to death on a cross
options.B: Demanded golden crowns in the Temple
options.C: Refused to associate with poor fishermen

explanation: Christ's supreme humility and selfless condescension serves as the blueprint for Christian unity and service.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In Colossians 3:18-21, Paul outlines Christian household relationships, instructing children to:

options.A: Obey their parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing to the Lord
options.B: Disregard parental guidance once they start working
options.C: Command their parents to buy them chariots
options.D: Leave the home at age twelve

explanation: Filial obedience in the home brings divine blessing and reflects spiritual order.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18, Paul comforts believers concerning departed saints, assuring that at Christ's Second Coming:

options.A: The dead in Christ will rise first, and then the living will be caught up together in the clouds to meet the Lord
options.B: Only the twelve apostles will enter heaven
options.C: The world will continue without end
options.D: Departed souls are reincarnated as animals

explanation: The Blessed Hope assures resurrection victory for departed believers and reunion at the Parousia.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: In 1 Peter 2:9, believers in Christ are celebrated with which elevated spiritual titles?

options.A: 'A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people'

explanation: 1 Peter 2:9 proclaims the royal priesthood and sacred calling of the redeemed church.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The first Protestant Christian mission established in Badagry, Nigeria in September 1842 was founded by:

options.A: Rev. Thomas Birch Freeman of the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society

explanation: Freeman arrived in Badagry in 1842, establishing the Methodist mission followed closely by Henry Townsend (CMS).
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Samuel Ajayi Crowther is celebrated in Nigerian Christian history as the:

options.A: First African Anglican Bishop (consecrated in 1864) who translated the Bible into Yoruba
options.C: Founder of the Cherubim and Seraphim church

explanation: Crowther led the Niger Mission and translated the Bible and Book of Common Prayer into Yoruba.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Mary Mitchell Slessor, the Scottish Presbyterian missionary in Calabar, is famous for:

options.A: Eradicating the barbaric killing of twin babies and defending women's and children's rights
options.C: Building the first railway bridge over the Benue
options.D: Leading the Aba women's protest against taxation

explanation: She lived among the Efik and Ibibio, adopting abandoned twins and stopping human sacrifice.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The Church Missionary Society (CMS) established Nigeria's first secondary grammar school in Lagos in 1859, known as:

options.A: CMS Grammar School, Lagos

explanation: CMS Grammar School was founded in June 1859 by Rev. Thomas Babington Macaulay.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Christian missionary societies contributed immensely to socio-economic development in Nigeria through:

options.A: Establishing Western schools, training colleges, modern hospitals, and leper colonies
options.B: Mining gold bullion exclusively for European kings
options.C: Banning indigenous agricultural crops like yams
options.D: Preventing Nigerians from learning reading and writing

explanation: Missions built literacy, established healthcare clinics, and developed written orthographies for indigenous languages.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The indigenous African Independent Churches (Aladura churches) emerged in Southwestern Nigeria primarily to:

options.A: Incorporate African spiritual expressions, fervent prayer, divine healing, and indigenous music
options.D: Enforce the Latin language in Sunday liturgy

explanation: The Aladura movements (Christ Apostolic Church, Cherubim & Seraphim, Church of the Lord) met deep spiritual needs through prayer and healing.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Apostle Joseph Ayo Babalola is celebrated as the charismatic evangelist who led the:

options.A: Great 1930 Revival at Oke Oye, Ilesa, leading to the rapid expansion of Christ Apostolic Church (CAC)
options.B: Founding of the Roman Catholic mission in Onitsha
options.C: Establishment of the Seventh-day Adventist hospital in Ile-Ife
options.D: First translation of the Bible into Hausa

explanation: The 1930 revival sparked unprecedented spiritual awakening, miraculous healings, and the eradication of occult shrines.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Father Joseph Shanahan (the Apostle of Eastern Nigeria) transformed Catholic evangelization in Igboland through:

options.A: Using rural primary and secondary bush schools as the primary vehicle of conversion and social advancement
options.B: Imposing French language in local village courts
options.C: Purchasing commercial river steamboats on River Niger

explanation: Shanahan recognized that village schools attracted youth, educating and converting entire generations across Igboland.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) was established in 1976 as an umbrella ecumenical body to:

options.A: Promote Christian unity, defend religious freedom, and liaise with the government on national issues
options.B: Form a single political party to contest general elections
options.C: Abolish all denominational differences in doctrine

explanation: CAN unites Catholic, Protestant, Pentecostal, and African Indigenous churches to defend Christian welfare and advocate peace.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum

question: Inter-religious dialogue in a multi-faith country like Nigeria promotes:

options.A: Mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, and collaboration for national development
options.B: The violent suppression of minority religious groups
options.C: The compulsory unification of all sacred scriptures

explanation: Peaceful dialogue through bodies like NIREC (Nigeria Inter-Religious Council) de-escalates conflict and strengthens national unity.
syllabus: Current JAMB UTME / WAEC SSCE Curriculum
